text: include the following: 1) Incoming Utility Supply: Additional main incoming supply lines from TECO may be required if the initial feed is not rated for the maximum site load post-expansion. Incoming power transformers will be insufficient for maximum load and an additional Power Transformer will be required for each train bringing the total to 8. Note if incoming power transformers include capacity for expansion, it may be possible to limit the number of additional units to 3. Gas Insulated Switchgear will increase in size / number / complexity. 2) 13.8 kV Power Distribution: Each 13.8kV bus will need to be expanded to accommodate additional feeders and VFDs. 3) 480V Power Distribution: An expansion of switchgear and distribution equipment is necessary to feed the new users 4) Incoming Pipeline: It is anticipated that an additional pipeline will be required to provide the additional CO feeding the plant, or the initial trunk pipeline within the “last mile” of the plant is to 2 originally be sized for greater than 2 mtpa. If an additional pipeline is to be added in future expansion phases, space must be allocated in any right of way utilized or created for the initial pipeline. 5) Traffic: Additional shipping and unloading activities may increase risk of collision or necessitate additional safety systems. 6) Noise: Additional fan coolers will increase noise level around the facility. 7) Proximity to LPG Terminal: The plant will expand towards the LPG Terminal and may be more exposed to fire and blast events emanating from that location. 8) Additional Personnel: An increase in plant size or complexity will increase the required number of operations personnel, which might drive need for additional shelters etc. 9) Berths: The number of required loading berths is driven by the frequency of cargo operations and loading rate. At 2mtpa and the base vessel loading rate of 1,250 m3/h the time between a vessel departing from the berth and the next one starting mooring operations is 69 hours. Increasing the vessel loading rate to 2,000 m3/h increases the margin to 75 hours. At 8mtpa there will be less than an hour between one vessel departing and the next one mooring. Increasing the vessel loading rate will increase this interval to 7 hours. This still provides insufficient margin and therefore a second berth would be recommended. Page43 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version There is enough room at the site to comfortably add a second berth in association with future throughput expansion. There may even be enough room to add a third berth as shown in Figure 3.18. Figure 3.18: Potential future berths to accommodate throughput expansion. Expansion outside the planned initial fence line is also possible with the potential to expand total CO 2 throughput in the immediate area to far beyond 8 mpta. Figure 3.19 shows parcels in dark blue that are currently vacant and available as of the writing of this report (from Port Tampa Bay’s website). It is conceivable that, for example, an identical hub to T-RICH could be built on the same-sized parcel directly to the north.
